design:
**D1. The window carries its own relaunch identity.** Before the window is shown, the app writes four shell properties on it: app identity, relaunch command (the same command the desktop shortcut runs), display name 'AgentWeave', and icon (the packaged app icon). Spike, 2026-11-04: all four set on a test window were read back from a separate process with SHGetPropertyStoreForWindow, so the acceptance drive can check them without a human. Pinning such a window uses these properties (Windows' documented relaunch behaviour). The pin click itself stays an operator check. The CLI's own code imports only the standard library, so this is done through ctypes, not pywin32. Rejected: a Start-menu shortcut carrying the app identity. It also works and slice 4 (notifications) may need one, but it is more install-time machinery than the pin needs, so it is deferred to slice 4.

**D2. One window per Hub, focused by the launcher.** The window markers that already exist per port (cli.py:1547) say a window is open and which process owns it. A launch that finds a live marker for its Hub restores and brings that window to the front itself, then exits. A process just started by the operator's click is allowed to take the foreground. Rejected: asking the owning process to focus itself through a file or pipe, which adds a channel and still hits the foreground rules.

**D3. Window geometry is the launcher's, stored beside the window's storage.** Size, position and maximized state are saved when the window closes and passed to the window at creation. If the saved position is off every connected screen, the window falls back to the primary screen.

**D4. Close asks the Hub, then stops it through the existing stop path.** pywebview's `closing` event can cancel a close. On close, the app asks the Hub one instance-wide question: what work is running (agent turns, check runs, landings, builds not ended, across projects). With nothing running, the close goes ahead and the same code `agentweave stop` uses stops the Hub. With work running, the close is cancelled and the page shows the three-way prompt. 'Stop it all' runs the stop path; 'keep running' closes the window only; 'cancel' does nothing. If the Hub cannot be reached, the window closes and the Hub is stopped as when idle, since there is nothing left to protect. Rejected: deciding in the page alone, which cannot see other projects' work.

**D5. The rollback setting is the launcher's.** 'Closing the window leaves AgentWeave running' is stored beside the window geometry (D3), because the launcher must read it before it asks the Hub anything, and is shown under App settings, where the page reads and writes it through the window. Off by default.

**Hazard (Tier 2).** Closing the window now stops the Hub and, after 'Stop it all', the agents' runs. On the operator's :8000 this reaches live work, and :8000 runs this checkout, so the new close takes effect there at its next restart; the UI prompt reaches it on its next reload. It replaces an agreed requirement (app-lifecycle n6). Mitigations: the instance-wide work check before any stop; a Hub that cannot answer is never taken as idle while it is still up (the page asks again rather than guessing); a close stops only its own port's Hub (FR on own-hub), since :8000 and :8010 run side by side on this machine; every drive runs on a scratch port with the trial profile, never :8000 or :8010. Rollback: the D5 setting restores today's behaviour without a release.

open_questions.question: Does an enabled job or loop that is not a build count as work? Operator 2026-11-04: no; they just miss their firings.

problem: The operator, 2026-11-04: 'I don't want to have a terminal open and then close the app, run agentweave stop, then agentweave again, then maximize it.' Pinning the app to the taskbar shows a Python icon. The process sets its own app identity (src/agentweave/cli.py:1095-1109, 'AgentWeave.Hub'), but nothing tells Windows how to relaunch it, so the pin falls back to pythonw.exe. Closing the window leaves the Hub running by design (app-lifecycle n6-closing-the-window-leaves-the-hub-running; cli.py:1352-1355), so getting a fresh Hub takes a terminal. The window keeps page storage (cli.py:1147) but not its size, position or maximized state.

requirements.statement: While the app window is open, its taskbar button shows the name AgentWeave and AgentWeave's icon, never Python's.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-04: pinning showed a Python symbol. A pin that relaunches Python is useless as a way to open the app.
requirements.statement: Pinning the open window's taskbar button produces a pin with AgentWeave's name and icon. Clicking that pin with the app closed opens AgentWeave exactly as the desktop shortcut does, and with the app open it focuses the open window.
Opening, using and closing the app from the desktop shortcut or a pin never shows a console or terminal window.

A launch (shortcut, pin, or bare `agentweave`) while the app window is open for the same Hub opens no second window and starts no second Hub. It brings the open window to the front, restored if it was minimized.
A launch while the Hub is running in the background with no window open opens a window on that Hub without restarting it, so work it is running continues uninterrupted.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-04: having to maximize the window again on every start is part of the friction.
requirements.statement: The window reopens at the size and position it had when last closed, and maximized if it was closed maximized. If that position is not on any connected screen, it opens on the primary screen at its remembered size.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-04: close means stop. Supersedes app-lifecycle n6-closing-the-window-leaves-the-hub-running.
requirements.statement: Closing the window when no work is running stops the Hub without asking. Within 30 seconds no Hub process for that port remains and the port is free.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-04: closing must never silently kill a build that was forgotten.
requirements.statement: Closing the window while work is running does not close it at once. It names what is running (how many agent turns, check runs and builds) and offers three choices. Stop it all and close: the work is stopped as `agentweave stop` stops it today, then the Hub. Keep running in the background: the window closes and the Hub and its work continue. Cancel: nothing changes.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-04: recurring jobs that are not builds just miss their firings while the Hub is stopped. Counting them would make closing nearly always ask, which defeats close-means-stop. A build counts even between firings because it holds tasks in flight.
requirements.statement: Work is running when any of the following is in progress for any project on that Hub: an agent turn, a check run, a landing, or a build (flow) that has not ended, even between its firings. An enabled job or loop that is not a build, with no turn in progress, is not work.

requirements.rationale: The operator's Hub on :8000 and the trial Hub on :8010 run side by side on this machine; a close of one must never reach the other.
requirements.statement: Closing a window, with any choice, stops at most the Hub serving that window's port. A Hub on another port of the same machine keeps running, with its processes and its work untouched.

requirements.rationale: The rollback for the Tier 2 hazard, with no release needed.
requirements.statement: The operator can turn on 'Closing the window leaves AgentWeave running' in the app's settings. It is off by default. While it is on, closing the window closes only the window, asks nothing and leaves the Hub and its work running, as before this change; the choice survives a restart of the app.

in_scope: Windows, the native app window (pywebview), started from the desktop shortcut, a taskbar pin, or bare `agentweave`.
The taskbar button's name and icon, and what a pin launches.
One window per Hub: a launch while it is open focuses it.
Remembering the window's size, position and maximized state.
What closing the window does to the Hub, with and without work running, and a setting that restores today's behaviour.
non_goals: The browser fallback when pywebview is unavailable (its behaviour is unchanged).
`--no-detach` foreground starts (unchanged: Ctrl+C stops them, no native window).
A tray icon, a Start menu entry as a feature, and starting with Windows.
Keeping recurring jobs that are not builds alive: they miss their firings while the Hub is stopped (operator, 2026-11-04).

summary: Slice 1 of 'AgentWeave feels like a desktop app'. On Windows, AgentWeave shows its own name and icon in the taskbar, and a pin reopens AgentWeave rather than Python. A launch while it is open brings back the open window, and the window reopens at the size, place and maximized state it was left in. Closing the window stops the Hub when nothing is running, and asks first when work is. No terminal at any point.
